# Copy review feedback: home and hydronic overview

**Reviewer:** Marketing & Growth agent
**Date:** 21 August 2026
**Scope:** `index.html` and `hydronic/index.html` only, as briefed. Other pages were grepped for contradicting claims but not reviewed.
**Filed here rather than in `.claude/copy-review/`** because that folder is regenerated by `npm run copy:dump` and this is not derived from the HTML.

Findings are `path:line`, current text, proposed replacement. Nothing was edited and nothing deployed. Items already open in `DECISIONS.md` are listed separately at the end with their locations, not re-flagged as findings.

---

## The through-line

The 19 August homepage rebuild was good and it landed cleanly. The problem is that **it only landed on the homepage.** Three separate decisions were applied to `index.html` and never propagated to `hydronic/index.html`, so the two pages now argue with each other about batteries, about how the product is described, and about whether the intelligence "learns".

A visitor lands on home, reads a generous framing of their battery, clicks through to hydronic, and finds a comparison table telling them their battery is a fire risk. That is one scroll and one click apart.

Second theme: **two rules in the standing list are broken on the homepage specifically because of the 19 August rebuild.** Ordinal language was deliberately stripped sitewide on 13 August and the rebuild put it back. That is worth knowing before the next rebuild does the same thing again.

---

## Findings

### 1. The battery posture contradicts itself across the two pages

Highest-priority finding. The homepage was rewritten on 19 August to the "wrong tool, not the enemy" framing, per the standing rule. The hydronic comparison table was not.

**`hydronic/index.html:117-119`**
Current: `Fire risk` / `Yes` / `None`
Proposed: Delete the row entirely.

This is an absolute safety claim about named competitors' product category, it needs sourcing, and it is precisely the adversarial posture the standing rule bans. It also contradicts `index.html:146`, which now says only "No lithium" and lets the reader draw their own conclusion.

**`hydronic/index.html:112-113`**
Current: `Degradation` / `Fades within ~10 years`
Proposed: `Capacity over time` / `Loses capacity as it ages`

Same softening already applied on the homepage. Drops the specific timeframe, which is the part that invites a complaint.

**`hydronic/index.html:277`**
Current: "Thermal Dawn stores heat and cold directly, so your dawn solar becomes evening comfort without the conversion losses, degradation, or fire risk. It's infrastructure that lasts decades, not a battery that fades in 10 years."
Proposed: "Thermal Dawn stores heat and cold directly, so your dawn solar becomes evening comfort without the conversion losses. It's infrastructure built to last decades."

**Note the page also contradicts itself.** `hydronic/index.html:293-294` ("I already have a battery. Does this still help?") is the best statement of the correct posture anywhere on the site, and it sits forty lines below a table calling batteries a fire risk. Keep 293-294 exactly as written.

---

### 2. The homepage hero still carries the frame the homepage body abandoned

**`index.html:34`** and the meta description
Current: "Australian-made thermal storage that replaces your gas boiler and runs your heating, cooling, and hot water on solar you've already generated, for around half the cost of a home battery."
Proposed: "Australian-made thermal storage that replaces your gas boiler and runs your heating, cooling and hot water on solar you've already generated. One system instead of two."

The comment at `index.html:166` states the section below was deliberately "reframed from 'half the cost of a battery' to 'one system instead of two'". The hero was not updated, so the page makes the old argument at the top and the new one 130 lines later. This is an incomplete edit rather than the open D1 decision: whichever way D1 lands, these two blocks should agree with each other.

**`hydronic/index.html:281`**
Current: "Our target is around half the cost of a comparable lithium battery system for heating, cooling, and hot water, with no degradation and no replacement costs in 10 years."
Proposed: "Total installed cost depends on your home size, existing pipework and electrical setup. Book a free, no-obligation site assessment for a fixed quote."

Three problems in one sentence: the retired frame, an absolute ("no degradation"), and a ten-year figure sitting next to our own cost claim in a section about what we charge.

### 3. "No counting installs" is broken on the homepage, and it is a regression

The 13 August changelog records "Ordinal language removed sitewide". The 19 August rebuild reintroduced it.

**`index.html:146`**
Current: "Across our first two homes, the heat pump stayed off through the entire 5pm to 9pm peak on 59 of the last 63 evenings."
Proposed: "Across our Victorian homes, the heat pump stayed off through the entire 5pm to 9pm peak on 59 of the last 63 evenings."

**`index.html:366`**
Current: "Come and see the hardware, and ask us anything. Our first install is a few streets away."
Proposed: "Come and see the hardware, and ask us anything. One of our Melbourne installs is a few streets away."

**`hydronic/index.html:253`**
Current: "...Across both homes, on 59 of the last 63 evenings, the heat pump hasn't run at all between 5pm and 9pm."
Proposed: "...On 59 of the last 63 evenings, the heat pump hasn't run at all between 5pm and 9pm."

The count adds nothing to the claim and the sample size is already carried by "63 evenings".

### 4. The lazy-case-study paragraph was rewritten on home and left standing on hydronic

**`hydronic/index.html:253`** (the whole block)
Current: "Different homes, same system. Hawthorn is a radiator home and a deliberately complicated retrofit, the kind that teaches you the most. A Gippsland home on a concrete slab went in and out in two days and hasn't hiccuped since. That matters more than it sounds: one radiator home, one slab home, running the same hardware and the same software, configured per house. The Gippsland system tops the slab up whenever power is free or cheapest..."

Proposed: replace with the homepage's rebuilt version, `index.html:266-269`:

> **How it runs.** It charges when power is cheapest, whether that's a free window, your own solar, or late-night off-peak. Then it holds the heat and runs your house through the evening with the compressor off.
>
> Radiators or a concrete slab, it's the same hardware and the same software. You set your tariff and the temperature you want. It handles the rest.

The homepage version is roughly half the words and answers "will it work in my house" rather than narrating what happened to us. "The kind that teaches you the most" is a benefit to Thermal Dawn, not to the reader.

---

### 5. "Our AI optimises" and "the system learns your home" overstate shipped behaviour

**`hydronic/index.html:191-192`**
Current: "The system learns your home" / "Our AI optimises charging times based on your solar forecast, local weather, and your tariff schedule, so you're always comfortable and always on the cheapest possible energy."
Proposed: "It schedules around your tariff" / "The controls plan charging around your electricity prices, your solar forecast and the weather, so you're comfortable and running on the cheapest energy available that day."

Two issues. "Learns" is an adaptive-behaviour claim, and per the 17 August ruling it should not be used unless that behaviour is live in the shipped controls. "Always on the cheapest possible energy" is an absolute that a tariff edge case will eventually break. The homepage already uses the defensible version at `index.html:268`.

---

### 6. "For free" is true in one of the three charging modes the same page describes

**`hydronic/index.html:34`**
Current: "...delivering it through your existing radiators and underfloor heating, all evening, for free."
Proposed: "...delivering it through your existing radiators and underfloor heating, all evening."

**`hydronic/index.html:184`**
Current: "Heat your home for free at night"
Proposed: "Heat your home on stored energy at night"

`hydronic/index.html:143` correctly says the store charges on off-peak and that "you're still buying your heat at the cheapest rate on your tariff instead of the dearest". That is the honest version, and it is directly contradicted by "for free" twice above it. The free-midday-window case at `:147` is the only one where free is literally true.

---

### 7. Warranty durations appear on the pre-order pages

Outside the two pages briefed, but the standing rule says "no warranty duration is stated anywhere", so flagging the locations rather than proposing copy:

- `pre-order/index.html:67` "Extended warranty: +2 years beyond standard cover"
- `pre-order/index.html:90` "Warranty Standard Standard +2 years"
- `pre-order/founder-premium/index.html:60` "Extended warranty: +2 years beyond standard"
- `thank-you/founder-premium/index.html:30` "the extended warranty"
- `pre-order/terms/index.html:40` references "extended warranty" (**legal copy, flag only, do not reword**)

"+2 years beyond standard" is a relative duration attached to an undefined standard, which is arguably worse than naming a number: it promises a comparison the customer cannot make. `hydronic/index.html:298` uses the approved wording ("comprehensive warranty coverage") and is fine.

---

### 8. Fleet figures on the homepage do not match the audited canonicals

**`index.html:259-261`**
Current: `Saved $2,399` / `Gas never burned 49,207 MJ` / `CO₂ avoided 2,524 kg`

`DECISIONS.md` records the baked fallbacks as the 17 August audited canonicals: fleet $2,260 / 47,311 MJ / 2,426 kg. The source comment at `index.html:242` says these are "Nick's current readings, newer than the 17 Aug audit doc".

Both cannot be true. Either these are fallbacks, in which case they should match the audit, or they are live readings, in which case they should not be baked into the HTML at all.

**No replacement proposed.** Per the brief, measured figures get queried, not substituted. What needs checking is whether the Warragul box has actually taken the corrected config from `dd5a285`, because the pre-fix feed was over-crediting by $43.62 and rising about $1.30 a day. The gas figure is internally consistent with the daily rates; the dollar figure is the one to verify.

---

### 9. En-dash ranges, which the mechanical check does not catch

INDEX reports zero em dashes, correctly. It does not test en dashes, and house style writes ranges as "to".

- `hydronic/index.html:69` "3–5 years" → "3 to 5 years"
- `hydronic/index.html:74` "3–4 bedroom" → "3 to 4 bedroom"
- `hydronic/index.html:285` "3–5 years" → "3 to 5 years"

Also present on `hydronic/pricing/index.html:233` and elsewhere. Worth adding an en-dash counter to `copy:dump` so this stops needing a human.

---

### 10. Minor: jargon and consistency

**`hydronic/index.html:298`**
Current: "smart controls + app, remote monitoring & OTA updates (opt-in)"
Proposed: "smart controls and app, remote monitoring and software updates (opt-in)"

"OTA" is trade language. "Remote software updates" is the customer phrasing, per the 17 August ruling, and the ampersands are inconsistent with the rest of the page.

## What is working, and should not be touched

**`hydronic/index.html:138-158`, "Works with Your Solar. Works Without It Too."** The strongest section on either page. It kills the biggest disqualifier a reader can bring, does it in four short cases, and the free-midday-window paragraph is genuinely current on where retail tariffs are heading. Do not shorten this.

**`hydronic/index.html:293-294`**, the "I already have a battery" FAQ. The clearest statement of the correct battery posture anywhere on the site. If the comparison table above it gets rewritten, rewrite it towards this.

**`index.html:143-146`**, the battery reframe. Lands the argument without picking a fight.

**Origin scoping** is disciplined throughout both pages. `index.html:337` explicitly says the heat pump is sourced rather than built, which is exactly the rule and is rarer than it should be in this kind of copy.

**The peak window** reads 5pm to 9pm consistently on both pages. No 3pm or 4pm variants found.

---

## One thing worth deciding soon, not a finding

The homepage stat is "59 of the last 63 evenings", measured to mid-August. A fuller winter figure now exists in the claims register (row 1b), covering the whole season on a larger sample. It is a stronger number on every axis: bigger sample, harder test, and a timeframe a reader feels.

The site will also quietly go stale as it stands, since "the last 63 evenings" ages without anyone noticing. Either wire the stat to the same query that produces it, or diarise a refresh. The first is a small job and removes the problem permanently.
